newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on Midwest weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on Midwest weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on nearly ideal crop weather in the Midwest, traders said.
Meteorologists said Thursday rain should cover much of the western Midwest now through Friday, bringing moisture to the dry areas of western Iowa.
Traders said the condition of the U.S. corn crop likely was improving and said there were prospects for a bumper corn crop unless weather problems develop.
USDA Monday said as of Sunday the U.S. corn crop was 66 percent good to excellent, above the 65 percent from the previous week.
Prices were underpinned by gains in nearby soybean contracts and on export news.

USDA Thursday said during the week ended June 12 U.S. net export sales of old crop corn totaled 516,800 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes. But net export sales of new crop corn at 256,200 tonnes, was below expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Corn futures closed unchanged to two cents lower, with July down 1-1/4 at $2.65-1/4 a bushel and December down 1-3/4 at $2.43-1/2.
Cargill Inc sold nine million bushels of December, 2.5 million July and sold two million September, traders said. FIMAT Futures sold two million bushels of September, traders said.
Iowa Grain bought 3.5 million Decwember and LIT America bought 2.5 million December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 70,000 contracts, about the same as the 70,004 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 2,000 December $2.20 puts at 1-3/4 cents, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 600 December $2.50 calls at 9-1/2 cents and Lind Waldock sold 1,000 July $2.70 puts at 4-1/2 to five cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, below the 19,562 traded Wednesday.
